messages:
jordana: Heads up — CI judge-runner produced nondeterministic eval outcomes during the quantized model bring-up. Failing on our smoke suite, looks like labels sometimes get dropped. Need a tie-breaker + judge selection plan before we flip the feature on.

alex: Can you paste the log lines or a short repro?

jordana: Repro snippet from staging logs:
```
WARNING runner: dropped 12 labels while flushing batch, concurrency=16
File "/srv/runner/eval.py", line 423, in _flush
  raise BufferOverflow("dropped outputs")
```
Not sure if this is the new quantized judge or the runner itself.

maria: We've seen something like this — runner v0.9.2 had a buffer bug; PR runner#341 fixes it. Will re-run once deployed. Regardless, we still need an explicit tie-breaker and rubric for judge selection (bias checks + subgroup tests).

sam: Proposal for tie-breaker: use an ensemble of 3 judges (cheap quantized judge, mid-size calibrated judge, reference human-like judge). Weighted voting by calibrated confidence; if top margin < 0.08 abstain and route to human review. Keeps things auditable.

lee: +1. Also add a consistency check: rerun each example 3x with different RNG seeds; if judge flip-rate > 15% mark for manual review. Helps catch nondet quantized behavior.

alex: For quantized judges we MUST run a calibration sweep vs the human majority on our heldout eval set. Compute Brier score + ECE. Suggested pass threshold: ECE < 0.07 and top-label accuracy within 1.5% of float baseline.

jordana: CI gating idea: smoke tests must have ensemble agreement >= 90% on the knotty examples before we allow model promotion. Tie-breaker should be implemented in the eval runner so CI is deterministic. Fall back to golden human annotations from S3 if judge infra fails.

ci-bot: Deployed runner PR runner#341 to staging at 2026-04-12T14:22Z :rocket:

maria: I'll draft a short RFC for the rubric. It will include: explicit tie resolution order, subgroup fairness checks (race/gender/locale buckets), and an abstain policy.

sam: Quick caution: don't use raw judge confidence for tie-breaks unless you map it through a calibration function. Calibrated_score = platt_map(raw_conf) or isotonic.

jordana: I'll add a minimal pseudo implementation to the eval-harness PR for the tiebreaker: 
```python
# pseudo
votes = [j.predict_label(x) for j in judges]
counts = Counter(votes)
most, second = counts.most_common(2)
if most[1] - second[1] < MARGIN_THRESH:
    # close call -> use calibrated weighted scores
    scores = [calibrate(j, x) for j in judges]
    weighted = sum(w * s for w, s in zip(weights, scores))
    pick = argmax(weighted)
else:
    pick = most[0]
if confidence(pick) < ABSTAIN_THRESHOLD:
    route_to_human(x)
```

alex: LGTM. Also add metrics to the dashboard: judge_flip_rate, tie_rate, abstain_rate, subgroup_disparity, calibration_brier. These should be tracked per-judge and for the ensemble.

jordana: Action items assigned: maria -> RFC & fairness checklist, alex -> CI gating test and dashboard metrics, sam -> calibration sweep scripts + mapping, lee -> validate runner fix in stress tests. I'll merge the runner fix PR once staging is green.

maria: I'll include recommended thresholds and a short template for human review instructions in the RFC.

sam: One more: add a nightly job that computes judge-vs-human agreement on a rotating sample, log changepoints and alert if agreement drops > 3 std devs.

jordana: Great. I'll post the RFC link here when ready and create the eval-harness PR with the tiebreaker implementation. :thumbsup:
